commenti.body: I suppose that is an idea, though one that invites its own questions - what's up with the 572 days later, why are the parents upstairs doing nothing if this is simply a burglar and they're awake, etc. Plus, and your milage may vary on this own, I find trying to impose a literal story or direct 1:1 metaphor onto a movie like *Skinamarink* just makes the movie end up feeling smaller. For a movie this unique about a more abstract idea of a childhood nightmare and inversion of nostalgia, I think it works best by meeting it on its own terms rather than trying to decipher it into something more literal (like the more common ideas that it's a metaphor for the kid being a coma or parental abuse).

Heh. That's a fun conspiracy theory but I don't think it holds any water. The way I saw it, the Skinamrink was more symbolic, representing childhood fears and anxieties rather than an actual burglar looting the house - I mean, it's certainly scarier, isn't it, having a mysterious, shadowy figure materializing in your own home compared to the idea it might just want to pinch your copper pipes? The imagery used in the film is far too surreal and layered for such a straightforward interpretation in my opinion. Because really, why leave the valuables behind when those would fetch the highest prices? So no, I think we're in psychological territory here rather than dealing with some strangely considerate burglar in a supernatural disguise!
